clue.text: Secret second flight

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, ... means underhand or clandestine, like intrigue conducted out of sight
a back staircase is the servants' secondary flight of steps in a big house

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the adjective means furtive or clandestine, and the noun phrase names a rear staircase used by servants.

clue.text: Musician's single

definitions.meaning: informal for living as a bachelor, unmarried

explanation.definitionFit: The composer's surname, and an informal word for a bachelor's unmarried life.

clue.text: Behave as a business representative ought when speaking. '

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
an MP, a Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

indicators.note: the word ought is to be heard, not spelt, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: said aloud in British English it sounds like ort, a scrap of food

explanation.surface: Conduct yourself as a salesman should when talking.
explanation.walkthrough: ORT (a leftover scrap) sounds like 'ought' in British, non-rhotic speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To comport oneself is to conduct oneself, a formal word for acting in a certain manner.

clue.text: From the estate to Victoria on the coach?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: Victoria is a major London railway station
a wagon is a coach or carriage

explanation.surface: Travelling from a country estate to London's Victoria by coach.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a London railway terminus; the question mark flags it as one station among many.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is the British name for a car with a long rear load area, called a station wagon in America.

clue.text: Plant is able to break a shut-out

indicators.note: the word for able breaks into the other letters, splitting them
out here means disordered, so the word shut is rearranged

parts.note: can means is able

explanation.surface: A plant manages to break through a lockout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut-out' reads as a lockout, but 'out' is the anagram signal giving THUS, and 'to break' is the container signal for the word meaning able.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a Mediterranean plant whose leaves inspired Corinthian column decoration.

clue.text: Geometrical instruments dividers, probably

definitions.meaning: those who govern, as in 'divide and rule'

explanation.definitionFit: Straight-edges for drawing lines, and monarchs who govern by dividing their subjects.

clue.text: Girl loses her head to the younger brother

indicators.note: the girl's name drops its opening letter, its head

parts.note: Mabel is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is beheaded in some grim tale involving a younger sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abel is Adam's second son, the younger brother killed by Cain.

clue.text: Burst from large meal

explanation.definitionFit: A burst tyre, and slang for a huge feast where one eats to excess.

clue.text: Area of the original canal horse

indicators.note: original means novel, so the word canal is given a new form

parts.note: a Shire is a breed of heavy draught horse

explanation.surface: The region where the first canal was dug, with a carthorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' rearranges CANAL into LANCA. The surface nods to the Bridgewater Canal, Britain's first, in the north-west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is a county in north-west England, a region of the country.

clue.text: Like an improving story about honour coming first

indicators.note: the words before this phrase are placed at the front, ahead of the story

parts.note: C, for circa, is the abbreviation for about
OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour
a parable is a moral tale meant to improve its hearer

explanation.surface: A moralising tale that puts honour above all else.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparable means similar or equivalent, so it can stand in for 'like' as an adjective.

clue.text: He's a stupid fellow to start running

definitions.meaning: ..., as lights or engines do when they start operating

explanation.definitionFit: Read as one word it is slang for an oaf; split in two it is the phrasal verb for a machine coming into operation.

clue.text: Make tablewear. for this handsome dresser

parts.note: to fashion is to make
a plate is an item of tableware

explanation.surface: Producing crockery to fill a kitchen dresser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dresser' suggests kitchen furniture holding plates, but it means a person who dresses smartly.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashion plate is a stylish person who always wears the latest clothes.

clue.text: Priest finally gets round holy hat

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word Priest is taken

parts.note: O is round in shape
pi is informal for pious or holy

explanation.surface: A clergyman ends up wearing a round sacred headdress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holy hat' wants to be a mitre or similar; the hat is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi is a lightweight pith helmet worn against the sun in India.

clue.text: Army surrounds Catherine's place, say, in Spain

indicators.note: the army's letters go round the outside of the rest

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: the region's name is wanted only as it sounds, so the spelling may differ

parts.note: Catherine of Aragon, Henry VIII's first wife, came from the Spanish kingdom of Aragon

explanation.surface: Troops encircle the homeland of Henry VIII's first queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the homophone: ARRAGON (an old spelling Shakespeare uses) sounds like Aragon, and TA surrounding it gives the Catalan port; 'in Spain' is the definition, read as a place in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragona is a port city and province in Catalonia, so it lies within that country.

clue.text: So useless to a blower, this instrument? Certainly not!

parts.note: taken as written
US, short for unserviceable, is British slang for useless
the blower is British slang for the telephone

explanation.surface: An instrument that a player who blows into it surely finds useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blower' looks like the player; it is the telephone. The closing 'Certainly not!' denies the surface claim that the brass bass is useless to one who blows it.
explanation.definitionFit: The sousaphone is a large brass tuba that wraps round the player, used in marching bands.

clue.text: The food causes no cross language

parts.note: O, nil, means none or no
X is the shape of a cross
a tongue is a language

explanation.surface: Some dish apparently spares diners any angry words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross language' reads as bad temper, but cross is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: Ox tongue is a cut of beef offal, cooked and eaten as a meat dish.

clue.text: The roof covering yonder church

parts.note: yonder points to something over there, as 'that' does

explanation.surface: Pointing out the roofing on a distant church.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reed laid over a house top is a traditional roofing material.

clue.text: How remiss of French widow!

parts.note: de is French for of
a relict is an old word for a widow

explanation.surface: Exclaiming at a French widow's negligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Derelict can mean neglectful of duty, as in 'derelict in his obligations'.

clue.text: Children's pastime was recalled by first, witness

indicators.note: the witness word is put before the other piece

parts.note: to witness is to see

indicators.note: recalled, called back, means the word was is read backwards

explanation.surface: A child's game is remembered by an onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Children play on a balancing plank that tips up and down, one at each end.

clue.text: Token for a Sterne novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of a Sterne take a new order

explanation.surface: A keepsake in exchange for one of Laurence Sterne's novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like Tristram Shandy; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest is a pledge or token payment given as a sign of more to come.

clue.text: Ask again about key for the instrument

indicators.note: the request goes around the key

parts.note: to reorder is to request again
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: Asking about the key in which an instrument is played.
explanation.definitionFit: A recorder is a woodwind instrument, a type of end-blown flute.

clue.text: Upset girl burst into tears

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: tears means rips, so the word burst is torn up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A distressed girl suddenly began crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst into tears' reads as crying; 'into tears' rearranges BURST into STURB.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb is to unsettle or agitate someone, a verb meaning to perturb.

clue.text: Wine bottle for a service in church

indicators.note: the service is placed inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A wine vessel used at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' reads as worship; it is the RAF, one of the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass flask for serving wine at table.

clue.text: Nero's. page, was, unusually, a figure of some importance

indicators.note: the letters are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written, its S included

explanation.surface: The emperor Nero's young attendant was oddly important.
explanation.definitionFit: A personage is a notable or distinguished person, a VIP.

clue.text: There's a marked inclination here to knock: back a drink

indicators.note: to knock back is to drink, and back also tells us to read the words a and drink backwards

parts.note: to sip is to drink

explanation.surface: A place with a steep lean, where a drink is downed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock back' looks like gulping a drink; here it turns A SIP around. The marked inclination is the famous Leaning Tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city is famous for its leaning bell tower, so a noticeable tilt is found there.

clue.text: Clear a bed for small daughter

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Tidying a bed for a little girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To weed is to clear unwanted plants from a garden plot.

clue.text: Unfasten the duck cage.

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O
a pen is an enclosure, a cage

explanation.surface: Letting a duck out of its enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a lock or catch is to unlock it, the verb opposite of close.

clue.text: Grotesque representation of a face like Katisha's

definitions.meaning: in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, Ko-Ko says the elderly Katisha has 'a ... of a face'

explanation.definitionFit: An exaggerated portrait is the art sense; the Mikado line applies the same word to an ugly visage.

clue.text: Petty officer holds the painter

indicators.note: the word Petty holds the painter's name within it

explanation.surface: A petty officer has the painter in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside the first word only. William Etty was an English painter of nudes.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was a nineteenth-century English artist known for his nudes.

clue.text: You can shake down here — it should be comfortable!

definitions.text: You can shake down here — it should be comfortable!

parts.words: You can shake down here — it should be comfortable!
parts.note: a shakedown is a makeshift bed, so this is a soft place to sleep; the mattress is also something you shake to plump it

explanation.definitionFit: A mattress stuffed with plumage gives a soft, comfortable bed to sleep on.
